_description:
E-046: ml/recipes/f4r2-40M-nolonhold.json — the pentad baseline codec #415 trained and #427/#432 froze — with ONE field added, fsq_levels '8'. The codec's bottleneck stops being 32 continuous floats and becomes 32 dimensions of 8 levels each: [8]^32, 3.000 bits/dim, a 96-bit codebook (2^96), FSQ per arxiv 2309.15505 with the bound as tanh on the raw pre-quantization activation (sigma 1, so the scale is learned into to_z), the gradient passed straight through the round, and NO codebook parameter, commitment loss, EMA or dead-code machinery. Every other field — tensor, d_z, patch, 512x12, 4 heads, d_dec 256, anomaly, batch 512, holdout_lon '0,0', head_probe true — is f4r2-40M-nolonhold's, field for field, so this recipe is a ONE-VARIABLE change against the codec every published pentad number stands on. 

HYPOTHESIS. E-045-A9 (#446) fired the pre-registered E-046 gate at 01:30Z on 2026-08-24: with the HEAD's input alphabet snapped to 8 levels per dimension (--input-quant 8, ml/temporal.py, E-044c) the 20,000-step one-step ratio read 0.4916 (z_mse 10.4486 / persistence 21.2544) against the 0.50560 / 0.50447 control pair — 0.0135 below the pair mean and about 12x the pair's own |Δ|, with rapid_r_kfold 0.677 [0.624, 0.725] inside the control band. Discretizing what the head READS helps one-step. This recipe moves THE SAME ALPHABET one stage earlier, into the codec, so the embedding the whole programme consumes is a finite alphabet rather than a vector the head has to be protected from. If the mechanism is input compression, doing it in the codec should reproduce A9's gain and additionally make it free downstream — nothing after the codec changes shape, because a quantized embedding is still a float vector of width d_z (plan §3). 

FALSIFIER (plan §6, and the arm STOPS at it). The stage-2 one-step ratio at 20,000 steps, against #427's trajectory on the SAME tensor, the SAME 206.5M xl144+znoise head geometry and the SAME protocol — final ratio 0.50560, and its 20,000-step point MUST BE READ OFF ml-metrics run-427.jsonl rather than remembered. FSQ passes only if it is CLEARLY below that point, not within the noise of it; the pentad pair #427/#432 measures that noise at |Δ| 0.00113, so 'clearly' has a number behind it. At or above the control, the bottleneck's continuity was not the binding constraint, the retrain is answered for about $9, and the arm stops. Second, softer read-out: does the unforced roll stop mode-locking to the calendar (the E-044c longstart: multi-context-end discriminator)? If a FSQ head's peaks still land on the same calendar months regardless of context end, quantization changed the input alphabet and not the failure. 

d_z STAYS AT 32, AND THIS RECIPE IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE PLAN'S OPTION A. ml/plans/E046_fsq_codec.md §4(a) recommends the paper's 2^14 configuration [8,8,8,6,5] at d_z 5. Two measurements made after that plan was written overrule it. (1) The round-6 reconstruction audit found 40 channels ALREADY squeezed at d_z 32: the codec's round trip collapses on Argo-carrying bins at FVU 15-18% against 0.4-0.5% on Argo-free bins, precisely because 40 channels compete for 32 dimensions. Shrinking to 5 dimensions compounds a known failure instead of testing the hypothesis, and the plan's own §8 lists 40 -> 5 (an 8x channel-to-dimension ratio, where the monthly anchor runs 39 -> 64) as its strongest open question. (2) A9 measured the winning alphabet on the SAME 32-dimensional z. [8]^32 is what was measured; [8,8,8,6,5] at d_z 5 is not. Changing the alphabet AND the width in one arm would confound them and no single result could attribute the difference. ONE VARIABLE. The paper's small-codebook configurations stay runnable through the identical flag — '--fsq-levels 8,8,8,6,5' with d_z 5 — as a later arm if this one moves. 

WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE. One codec retrain, ~20 h and ~$6 (the #415 class: 197,428 steps x 512 on the pentad tensor). The tensor is unchanged (family4_na025_pentad_r2, sha256 37e146384b…). ml/temporal.py is untouched — it receives [T, P, d_z] floats and that the values now live on a lattice is invisible to it, which is what makes this a codec-side change rather than a programme-wide one. The embed cache key changes BY ITSELF and correctly: codec_weight_hash is an md5 over the codec's first four weight tensors, so a new codec is a new hash and a new cache name. Budget the 8.5 h embed (MEASURED, #423) for the first stage-2 run on it. FSQ adds NO parameters, so the run's params_M is #415's 37.976M to the byte — which is exactly why ml/model.py:codec_from_ckpt reads fsq_levels back out of every checkpoint and REFUSES any fsq_* argument it does not implement: a loader that dropped the bottleneck would build a model whose state_dict loads cleanly and whose every z is a different function of the input, and nothing in its output would say so. 

WHAT A POSITIVE RESULT WOULD NOT ESTABLISH, said in advance (plan §6): n=1 on a new codec and a new bottleneck. ml/CLAUDE.md §3b's harder clause applies — the first result at a tier buys its own replication — so a seed-1 arm is required before any number off this recipe is written as a level rather than a first reading.
_provenance: Copied field for field from ml/recipes/f4r2-40M-nolonhold.json (the recipe #415 ran, whose checkpoint run-415 is the frozen codec under #423, #427, #432 and the whole E-045 ladder), adding exactly one key: fsq_levels '8'. That recipe's own provenance carries the architecture's lineage — f4r2-40M -> f4-40M, params 37,976,465, the 2026-08-19 holdout decision, and the '0,0' rather than 'none' reasoning (twelve eval scripts under ml/ still float() ck['args']['holdout_lon']). The FSQ half has one measurement behind it and one specification: the measurement is E-045-A9 (#446, 20k ratio 0.4916 against the 0.50560/0.50447 pair, 2026-08-24), and the specification is ml/plans/E046_fsq_codec.md, written 2026-08-22 and priced at ~$9 to a first verdict. The quantizer is ml/model.py:InputQuant — the SAME object #446 ran, not a second copy: E-046 moved it from ml/temporal.py into ml/model.py (the module both callers import) and gave it a zero_passthrough flag, because the head side must keep an exact 0.0 exact (a zero in a stencil slot is an ABSENT NEIGHBOUR, and an even L has no zero level) while the codec's bottleneck has no such convention and must round like any other value. NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN AT THIS CONFIGURATION. This recipe is the dispatch surface; its _description becomes a measurement when the run lands. DISPATCH WITH resume EMPTY — a fresh codec; run-415's continuous bottleneck is a different architecture and adopting its args on resume would be refused by ml/train.py's ARCH contradiction check, which is the correct answer.
